chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
question_text: Define vector product. Explain the properties of a vector product with two examples.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 7 SHORT ANSWER 2. The split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher. AP appearance: asked on the AP Inter 1st-year Physics paper, March 2026 (Section C, the first paper of the new 85-mark NCERT pattern) — transcription evidence, claim until the official paper PDF confirms the question number.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The definition
lines: The vector product of two vectors is a
vector whose magnitude is the product
of their magnitudes and the sine of the

lines.text: P × Q = PQ sin θ · n̂

lines: n̂ is perpendicular to the plane of P
and Q, by the right-hand rule.
steps.margin_note: Three parts to the definition: magnitude, direction, and the rule that fixes the direction.
steps.why: The direction clause is what makes it a VECTOR product — without n̂ and the right-hand rule the definition describes only a number.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the perpendicular direction, which reduces the definition to the magnitude alone.

recall.must_convey: That P × Q = PQ sin θ n̂, with n̂ perpendicular to the plane by the right-hand rule.
accept: P Q sin theta n cap

steps.memory_tip: Say all three parts: magnitude AB sin θ, the direction n̂, and the right-hand rule that fixes it.

steps.label: The properties

lines.text: P × (Q + R) = P × Q + P × R

steps.margin_note: Four numbered properties, each with its one-line equation. Note property 1 keeps the magnitude — only the direction flips.
steps.why: Properties 3 and 4 are just sin θ at its two extremes; 1 is the right-hand rule read in the other order. Nothing here needs memorising if the definition is understood.
common_mistakes: Writing P × Q = Q × P — the cross product anti-commutes.
Saying parallel vectors give the MAXIMUM product; that is the perpendicular case.

recall.must_convey: At least three properties: anti-commutative, distributive, zero for parallel, maximum for perpendicular.

steps.memory_tip: Four properties from two facts: the right-hand rule read backwards gives A×B = −B×A; sin θ at 0° and 90° gives the parallel and perpendicular cases.

steps.label: Two examples
steps.margin_note: The question says WITH TWO EXAMPLES — the pair τ and L is the expected answer and costs two lines.
steps.why: Both examples are position crossed with something — force gives torque, momentum gives angular momentum. Rotation runs on cross products.
common_mistakes: Giving work W = F·S as an example — that is the DOT product.

recall.must_convey: That torque = r × F and angular momentum = r × p are the two examples.
accept: angular momentum is r cross p
reject: P Q sin theta n cap

steps.memory_tip: Both examples start with r: r × F is torque, r × p is angular momentum.

insider_note: The properties carry 2 of the 4 marks, so list four of them. Two properties reads as a half answer.
